summary:
D.C. statehood advocates are intensifying their push ahead of the midterm elections, with efforts to build support among states and secure commitments from federal lawmakers. Recent events including federal intervention in D.C. governance and the deployment of National Guard troops have prompted advocates to argue that statehood is increasingly urgent for protecting local autonomy. Separately, advocates are working to defend D.C.'s fiscal independence against what they characterize as congressional overreach.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.

articles.title: Eyeing the midterm elections, D.C. is taking the fight for statehood to the states
